text: The project focuses on physical risk reduction at four high-risk glacial lakes, expansion of early warning systems specific to GLOF risks, and the use of eco-engineering and nature-based solutions. It is designed with a gender-responsive approach and aims to institutionalize climate risk management from community to national levels. The project covers over 11,000 km² and aligns with Nepal's National Adaptation Plan and updated Nationally Determined Contributions. It serves as a replicable model for mountain adaptation and aims to catalyze co-financing towards a total of nearly US$50 million.

metadata.solution_name: FP272: Protecting livelihoods and assets at risk from Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs) and climate change-induced flooding in glacial river basins of Nepal
